chapter: Philadelphia and the McRae Brothers Band, 1908-1929
title: Moving the band to New York; Barron's and radio broadcasts
summary: After Atlantic City the band came to New York, played Barron's on 129th Street and did supper-music broadcasts that listeners took for a white band.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: No, I didn't bother the piano. I really didn't bother too much with the piano. Just a little bit I could play it, but I didn't bother with the piano at all. After we put this band together, we went there -- we moved into New York. That was on the 29th. I think that was 1929 when we came to

The fall of '29. I think the summer of '29 when we played Atlantic City. That was the summer of '29 -- 1929. We came into New York of the winter of -- like September. You know, after Atlantic City closed we came into New York with the band. We played 129th Street. It was a private club -- Barron's. Was a 129th Street and Lenox downstairs there was a club. It was a private club. It was put up by these real estate fellows. They had released it out to just people at formal dances and things. We played like four or five days there -- it was night. Then we played at -- There was another place we were doing. We were broadcasting over -- Nola I know a studio had a broad -- I think it was NBC or CBS up there on the top floor, 111 (inaudible) 57th Street -- Nola know it was a studio up there.

But that was a big studio broadcasting. We worked there every night. We used to broadcast every night from 5:30 to 6.
And we were broadcasting everyday there. You know, like supper music -- what you call supper music.
And we had this beautiful band --
And we were broadcasting and people didn't know -- they really didn't know -- they only heard the band --
They probably didn't know it was a colored band or a white band, because the band was smooth pretty band with all the saxophones.
We used to have like E-flat soprano, B-flat soprano, C melody, and a clarinet. We give you the sound of real high voices. Real pretty high voices.
And we would start off like that and then we would go -- gradually go down to the four saxophones and come back to the clarinet and the muted
